text:
The candidate hypothesis introduces concepts—specifically "human capital" (measured by educational attainment and skill indices) and interaction terms moderating the effects of electricity consumption and GDP growth—that are neither mentioned nor investigated in the provided evidence. The actual study focuses on the direct relationships between ecological footprint, electricity consumption, real GDP, trade openness, urbanization, and life expectancy using quantile regression and spectral Granger-causality tests.

VERDICT: REJECT
